explanation: If every philosopher takes a differently named left fork first, a circular wait is possible. Numbering the physical forks gives every worker one common order: acquire the lower-numbered needed fork, then the higher-numbered one. A waiting chain must then move strictly toward larger fork numbers, which cannot form a cycle. Hold both through Eat, then release both; independent nonadjacent philosophers may still eat concurrently. C++ borrows ForkContext& and uses std::min/std::max on distinct adjacent indices. Actual std::thread workers share only the provided locked fork state; the user method neither deletes the context nor owns its lifetime.
correctness: Every successful iteration acquires both distinct adjacent forks through exclusive locks before Eat, and releases each afterward, so mutual exclusion and per-philosopher fork requirements hold. When a worker blocks holding one fork, it holds the lower and waits for the higher. A circular wait would require strictly increasing fork numbers around a cycle, impossible in a finite ordered set. Thus deadlock cannot occur. Under eventual scheduling, a worker at the end of any waiting chain completes its finite Eat and releases forks; repeated progress with finitely many requested iterations lets every worker finish. The loop calls Eat exactly bites times for its own role and zero times when bites=0. Release order does not affect the increasing acquisition invariant.
walkthrough: For three philosophers and one bite each, role 0 needs forks 0 and 1; role 1 needs 1 and 2; role 2 needs 2 and 0. All use increasing physical order, so role 2 takes 0 before 2. One possible schedule lets role 0 take 0/1, eat and release; then role 1 takes 1/2 and eats; then role 2 takes 0/2 and eats. The observed transcript [0,1,2] is valid, but [2,1,0] or another safe order is also accepted. With four philosophers, roles 0 and 2 may eat concurrently because their fork pairs are disjoint.
timeComplexity: O(bites) fixed synchronization/eating calls per worker, O(philosophers*bites) total algorithmic calls. Blocking/scheduler waiting and opaque eating duration are excluded; no fixed elapsed-time or starvation-latency bound is claimed.
spaceComplexity: O(philosophers) shared fork-lock state provided by the judge, O(1) local algorithm storage per worker, excluding native thread stacks and private observed transcript.
edgeCases: Two philosophers need the same pair of distinct forks.
Zero bites and repeated independent cases.
Wraparound role must order forks 0 and philosophers-1 by physical number.
Only adjacent fork ownership permits eating; all locks must be released at return.
Different eating/release orders remain valid if safety and completion hold.
